newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen mixed ahead of trade data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen mixed ahead of trade data.

text.p: Singapore shares are likely to mark time in a mixed climate on Tuesday ahead of the release of April non-oil export figures at noon, dealers said.
A Reuter poll of eleven economists on Monday had forecast a meagre rise of 0.5 percent, a flat outlook for the economy.
"Traffic has been light because of the trade data and FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee). There are lots of good excuses for waiting," a local brokerage dealer said.
The Singapore key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended down 9.56 points at 2,050.94 on light volumes on Monday.
Support for the index in the near-term was assessed around 2,030 and then 2,000 points, with the market expected to form a base around present levels.
Selected buying of blue chip stocks and speculation in new issues, such as Tye Soon, should again dominate actives until clearer direction is set upon the release of the trade data.
